current_answer: Cloudflare says active members on its older USD 5,000 Tier 3 or USD 250,000 Tier 1 cap may ask for a case-by-case evaluation when approaching the cap. An approved increase does not reset the original 12-month expiry. The current public tiers are USD 10,000, USD 100,000, and USD 350,000 in eligible Cloudflare credits, not cash; product caps, exclusions, payment method and post-credit billing still matter. For new self-funded Tier 3 applicants, the page still conflicts: the tier says no minimum funding, while its general checklist asks for funding within 12 months. NLnet still lists 3 November; Interledger Local Impact remains paused.

catalogue_card.question: Can an existing Cloudflare startup member get more credits?
catalogue_card.text: Some active members on the old USD 5,000 or USD 250,000 cap may request a case-by-case increase when nearing the cap. Approval is not automatic, and the original 12-month expiry does not reset. New self-funded Tier 3 applicants still face conflicting eligibility wording.

summary: Cloudflare allows active older-cap members nearing their limit to request an individual upgrade review; it does not extend their original year.
Current tiers are USD 10,000, USD 100,000 and USD 350,000 in eligible service credits, subject to product caps and exclusions.
The self-funded Tier 3 line still conflicts with Cloudflare’s general recent-funding checklist.
NLnet’s 3 November form remains open; Interledger Local Impact remains paused.
uncertainty: Cloudflare does not publish a numerical upgrade test or decision time; no existing member outcome was verified.
Cloudflare has not reconciled the Tier 3 self-funded line with its all-applicant recent-funding line.
Country coverage and account-specific billing are not established from the public page.
freshness_note: Checked 8 October 2026; older catalogue rows retain their own verification dates.
